issues.description: revoke_error exposed to API without sanitization despite author's own unresolved security question
issues.detail: The PR author asks in the description whether it is safe to display the revoke error; nobody answered. RevokeErr is a free-form string from backend revocation paths that can carry URLs, internal hostnames, credentials, or upstream API messages. Decide the contract: sanitize, gate behind a capability, or document the trust boundary. Do not merge a field whose safety the author is unsure of.

issues.description: Public API rename FetchLeaseTimes -> FetchLeaseInfo breaks external callers with no deprecation shim
issues.detail: FetchLeaseTimes is an exported method on ExpirationManager. Renaming in place breaks any out-of-tree consumer or fork vendoring vault internals. Keep FetchLeaseTimes as a thin deprecated wrapper that calls FetchLeaseInfo, or at minimum document the break in the changelog. Neither is done today.

issues.description: leaseInfoForExport leaks unexported namespace pointer into the redacted export struct
issues.detail: The exported leaseEntry now carries le.namespace by reference, not by value. Callers can observe (or mutate) live namespace identity through what is supposed to be a redacted snapshot. Either copy namespace.Path as a plain string into the response, or document the invariant that namespace is immutable post-registration.

issues.description: Test coverage for the new fields only asserts path; namespace_path and revoke_error are untested
issues.detail: TestSystemBackend_leases checks path == "secret/foo" and nothing else. The two genuinely new and risky additions, conditional namespace_path emission and the security-sensitive revoke_error, have zero coverage. Add a namespaced-lease test and a revoke-failure test that assert the response shape.

issues.description: OpenAPI schema and handler disagree on field presence conventions
issues.detail: path is declared Required but the handler can emit it empty; namespace_path and revoke_error are conditionally omitted while expire_time is set to nil then overwritten. Three different absence conventions in one response map. Pick one rule (always-present-with-zero or omit-when-empty) and make schema and handler agree.

issues.description: Rename half-applied: metric label expire.fetch-lease-times and test name still carry the old identifier
issues.detail: FetchLeaseInfo still emits the metric expire.fetch-lease-times, and TestExpiration_FetchLeaseTimesIrrevocable keeps the old name. The rename was meant to signal the function returns more than times; leaving old identifiers scattered re-complects the meanings the rename was trying to separate. Also: one test silently swapped nil for t.Context() with no stated reason.

synthesis.summary: The panel agrees: the patch is mechanically clean and the right shape, but it ships with the author's own unresolved security question about revoke_error exposure still in the PR body. That question is the design decision, not a footnote, and must be answered on the record before merge. The public method rename lacks a deprecation shim, the redacted export struct now leaks an unexported namespace pointer, and the response shape uses three different conventions for absent fields while the OpenAPI schema disagrees with the handler. Test coverage covers only the easy field; the two genuinely new and risky additions (namespace_path, revoke_error) are untested. Verdict: NEEDS-WORK on the contract and security layers, not the code.
